*(Refer to the comprehension passage in Question 11)*

How did a master navigator (*pwo*) deduce the presence of unseen landmasses?
options: By deciphering subtle interference patterns in ocean swells.
By utilizing early metallic compasses traded with Europeans.
By sending white terns ahead to fetch physical evidence of soil.
By consulting the electronic navigational equipment aboard the Hōkūleʻa.
questions.explain: The text directly provides this specific detail in the first paragraph: 'A master navigator... could deduce the proximity of unseen landmasses by deciphering the subtle interference patterns in ocean swells...'

questions.q:
*(Refer to the comprehension passage in Question 21)*

According to Dr. Amina Bello, what specific proof did the Nok civilization provide regarding the Iron Age?
options: That the Nok traded extensively with ancient Rome.
That indigenous technological innovation in Africa occurred without Eurasian influence.
That terra-cotta sculptures were only created for early European explorers.
That iron-smelting first began in 200 AD.
questions.explain: The text provides this explicit detail in Dr. Bello's quote: 'proving that indigenous innovation occurred completely independently of Eurasian influence.'

*(Refer to the comprehension passage in Question 41)*

According to the passage, why is *makuba* an essential component in the construction of the *soro*?
options: It acts as a structural reinforcement for the vaulted ceiling arches.
It provides a potent, waterproof seal when mixed with mud for mortar and plaster.
It naturally deters termites from eating the mud bricks.
It serves as a strong foundation layer that stops rising damp.
questions.explain: The passage explicitly details that the mortar and external plaster consist of mud mixed with *makuba*—which it describes as 'a potent, waterproof extract.'
